keyVerseDR: "Seek, and you shall find: knock, and it shall be opened to you." (Mt 7:7)

level1.title: This Week's Catholic Virtue: Curiosity
level1.story: Curiosity means being interested in new things and wanting to explore. God's world is full of wonders waiting to be found!
level1.heartIntro: Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice curiosity all week. On Saturday, talk together, write what you practiced, and a parent signs.
questions: What was the most interesting thing we discovered this week?
What do we still wonder about God's world?
actions: Hang this sheet on the fridge
level1.prayer: Jesus, fill me with wonder. Help me seek You in everything I learn. Amen.

activity.title: Daily Action Checklist
activity.intro: Color a star each day, Monday through Saturday. Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice with your family. A parent signs at the end of the week.
items: MON: Ask a grown-up one 'why' question
TUE: Look closely at a bug, leaf, or cloud
WED: Ask Grandma or Grandpa about their childhood
THU: Learn the name of a new animal
FRI: Ask a question about Jesus at dinner
SAT: Explore a new place in your yard or park

level2.title: This Week's Catholic Virtue: Curiosity
level2.story: Curiosity is a holy wondering. It means asking good questions, noticing new things, and wanting to explore God's world. Jesus told us to seek and knock. A curious heart wants to learn about plants, animals, people, and most of all about God. Curiosity grows when we ask, look closely, and listen for answers.
level2.heartIntro: Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice curiosity all week. On Saturday, talk together, write what you practiced, and a parent signs.
questions: What was the most interesting thing we discovered this week?
How did God help us grow in curiosity?
actions: Hang this sheet on the fridge
level2.prayer: Jesus, fill me with wonder. Help me seek You in everything I learn. Amen.

activity.title: Daily Action Checklist
activity.intro: Color a star each day, Monday through Saturday. Hang this sheet on the fridge and practice with your family. A parent signs at the end of the week.
items: MON: Look up the answer to a question you wonder about
TUE: Learn three facts about a saint
WED: Ask a family member about their work
THU: Find out how something at home works
FRI: Read about a country you have never visited
SAT: Ask a priest or catechist a faith question
